dedupe_keys.name: building footprints oldenburg derived from aerial imagery

description: This dataset contains about 78,000 building footprint polygons covering the whole city of Oldenburg in Lower Saxony, Germany, extracted from aerial imagery by deep-learning image segmentation. It was produced by Jonas Bostelmann and Mike Engel of the Lower Saxony state office for geoinformation and surveying (LGLN), which trained the model, as a test of automatic building detection for the state's mapping. Coverage is the administrative area of Oldenburg; a small metadata file records the processing run. Access: version 1.1 was published on Zenodo on 18 January 2024 as a GeoJSON file of about 72 MB. Licence: Creative Commons Zero, with no restrictions; free. Caveats: machine-derived outlines that can merge or miss buildings, unlike the official cadastral footprints (ALKIS) that LGLN also maintains. Simulation uses are building exposure layers for flood and heat studies, and comparison of automatic footprints with authoritative data for city digital twins. Related records: GlobalBuildingAtlas and the 3DBAG and EUBUCCO building datasets.
